title: When approval stops fitting
target_audience: AI-native operators building reviewable production systems

claims.text: Story and visual-direction approvals must match the exact carousel story content hash.
Carousel packaging requires final approval matching the exact current story hash.
The carousel contract blocks unapproved screenshots and generated media presented as evidence.

slides.question_answered: What goes wrong with ordinary approval states?
slides.headline: A green tick can outlive the thing it checked.

slides.question_answered: What does an approval belong to?
slides.headline: Here, approval belongs to one exact story.
slides.body: Source, claims, assets and slides are fingerprinted before review.

slides.question_answered: What happens when the story is edited?
slides.headline: Change one line and the fingerprint changes with it.

slides.question_answered: Can the old approval pass to the revision?
slides.headline: The old approval no longer fits.
slides.body: The decision stays on record. The revised story returns to review.

slides.question_answered: Where is the same rule applied?
slides.headline: Story, visual direction and final file are approved separately.

slides.question_answered: What does the extra review cost and protect?
slides.headline: Repeating the check adds friction.
slides.body: It stops an old decision travelling with changed work.

slides.question_answered: What is the reusable operating principle?
slides.headline: Good review expires with the version it checked.

editorial.strongest_reason_to_reject: The physical interlock may feel over-engineered if the exact approval mismatch is not legible without railway knowledge.
editorial.audience_payoff: Operators get one concrete test for whether human review remains attached to the work that was actually reviewed.
editorial.countercase: Exact reapproval adds friction after small changes, so the system should invalidate only the stages affected by the change.
